body: Hi, I'm a new member of @leotlee's team. Could I be added to the invite series for this via Jeff.Weiner@microsoft.com? I'll likely miss the CE(S)T-timed meetings, but will be available for the PT-timed meetings. Thanks!
Hey @AtOMiCNebula, you should now be added to all the invites!

Minutes:

- Base URLs Status Update: Anne van Kesteren requested a status update on base URLs from Dominic Farolino because communication on Matrix has been unreliable. Philip Jägenstedt agreed to ping Dominic Farolino on Matrix ([00:03:24](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.gj051woo9yi2)).
- HTML Streaming Methods Pull Request Stack Review: Noam Rosenthal reviewed a stack of four pull requests for new HTML streaming methods—including trusted type changes, positional methods, and stream HTML—to determine if they can reach stage three ([00:05:56](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.x8k1aal338kk)). Anne van Kesteren and Noam Rosenthal noted that Gemini and Claude were used to review the pull requests, and Simon and Anne van Kesteren approved them ([00:07:41](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.r2lsa0m2vhte)) ([00:09:33](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.rlo8pq681kij)). Because Mozilla had already agreed to stage 3, it was agreed to move this proposal to stage 3 at this time.
- Stage Three Label Updates for HTML Streaming: Philip Jägenstedt updated the labels to reflect the stage three agreement for the HTML streaming methods pull requests, while Noam Rosenthal committed to merging them one by one after verifying each set of tests ([00:13:12](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.l61jl984h8if)).
- Template Elements in SVG and MathML Namespaces: Noam Rosenthal and Ryosuke Niwa discussed an issue dating back to 2012 where partials of SVG and MathML inside templates parse incorrectly under the HTML namespace ([00:14:14](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.ca2kd6i5xnbb)). Ryosuke Niwa proposed solution C, where templates inside SVG or MathML elements receive an implicit type matching their container's parsing mode, combined with an optional explicit type attribute to override parsing modes when needed ([00:21:18](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.sg7pavgbi6ed)) ([00:24:37](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.jo19fz1wr06q)). Anne van Kesteren supported this approach to maintain a single template element across languages ([00:25:38](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.atnn0vhdyypp)), and Noam Rosenthal planned to propose a pull request while reaching out to the SVG and MathML working groups ([00:26:37](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.mjd7qpp9wjd3)).
- Declarative Shadow Roots and Template For Streaming: Ryosuke Niwa inquired about supporting template for features with declarative shadow roots. Noam Rosenthal clarified that templates inside a declarative shadow root stream into that shadow root if they are direct descendants, and race conditions with out-of-order streaming are intentionally left for userland to manage ([00:32:57](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.cnwxszoexw1f)) ([00:36:02](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.s92hygegfafp)).
- Switch Attribute Implementation in Chromium: Anne van Kesteren raised whether Microsoft implementing the switch attribute in Chromium changes Chrome's stance on the pull request ([00:36:54](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.92f5u4oveen)). Luke clarified from Open UI discussions that the pragmatic approach of using input type checkbox with the switch attribute was agreed upon, and browsers are supportive ([00:38:04](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.8xsa2wwp343b)).
- Future Meeting Schedule Adjustments: Philip Jägenstedt, Anne van Kesteren, and Luke discussed changing the meeting frequency to every other week to reduce the burden of US-friendly time meetings and accommodate European editors ([00:40:38](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.3pm9hign76v)). Sideshowbarker (Mike) noted constraints regarding time zones and mentioned that Ladybird contributors like Shannon and Zagi have been filing bug reports based on real spec issues ([00:43:01](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.9r48tkh74abr)) ([00:46:02](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.fzgzftqx9skp)).
- Form Ownership Specification Discrepancy: Luke reported finding a specification bug regarding how form ownership is handled, noting that browsers do not match the current spec behavior. Luke added this topic to next week's agenda for further discussion ([00:48:15](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.vwqkfqmn83sd)).
- Event Machinery and Reference Target Feature Clashes: Anne van Kesteren discussed plans to spec synchronous page hide removal and update event machinery, but noted that work must wait because the reference target feature impacts event retargeting and command semantics, potentially causing conflicts ([00:49:22](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1x5FdE-xhWkVMoPC8FCiTIu0c4lLR_3llsf8X0Afp4/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.bra4prq71hlb#heading=h.8arml8k03ehd)).
